name: Fasciolopsis buski

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: approximately 130–150 × 60–90 µm; large oval, yellow-brown, thin shell, subtle operculum, unembryonated when passed.
Large leaf-shaped adults inhabit the intestine.

transmission.detail: Eggs develop in water and infect snails; cercariae encyst on aquatic vegetation. Ingested metacercariae mature in the intestine.

life_cycle.detail: Larval stages develop in a snail.
Ingested metacercariae mature into intestinal adults.

hosts: Definitive: humans and pigs. Intermediate: freshwater snail; aquatic plants carry metacercariae.
distribution: Focal distribution in Asia, including parts of Southeast Asia; exposure to contaminated aquatic plants is relevant.
clinical_significance: Heavy infection can cause diarrhea, malabsorption, edema and intestinal obstruction.
diagnostics: Stool wet mount/concentration; 100× overview and 400× shell detail.
differential_diagnosis: Eggs strongly resemble Fasciola; intestinal versus hepatic disease cannot be inferred from an ambiguous egg alone.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
